definitions.explanation: An alcoholic beverage brewed from rice, water, and koji mold. The term specifically distinguishes traditional Japanese alcohol from foreign alcoholic drinks.

examples.japanese: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}を{一杯|いっぱい}ください。
この{日本酒|にほんしゅ}は{辛口|からくち}で{飲|の}みやすい。
examples.english: This sake is dry and easy to drink.

examples.japanese: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}は{冷|ひ}やでも{熱燗|あつかん}でも{楽|たの}しめるのが{魅力|みりょく}だ。
examples.english: The appeal of sake is that you can enjoy it chilled or hot.

notes:
USAGE:
{日本酒|にほんしゅ} specifically means sake brewed in the Japanese tradition, as distinct from {洋酒|ようしゅ} (Western liquor) or other foreign drinks. In casual speech, Japanese people often say simply お{酒|さけ} or {酒|さけ}, which can mean either sake specifically or alcohol in general depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日本酒|にほんしゅ}を{飲|の}む: to drink sake
- {辛口|からくち}の{日本酒|にほんしゅ}: dry sake
- {甘口|あまくち}の{日本酒|にほんしゅ}: sweet sake
- {熱燗|あつかん}: hot sake
- {冷|ひ}や / {冷酒|れいしゅ}: chilled sake

CULTURAL NOTE:
Sake brewing has a long history in Japan. Key terms include {純米酒|じゅんまいしゅ} (pure rice sake), {吟醸|ぎんじょう} (premium sake), and {大吟醸|だいぎんじょう} (super premium sake).
